title: Linear mixed model for repeated measurements
summary: The difference in rate of change between arms (treatment-by-time interaction) with a random intercept per patient, fitted by REML.

sizing._why: Sizing a slope difference needs the number of visits, their spacing and the within-patient correlation; no catalog form takes them. Simulation.

pinned_defaults: Both: REML named (REML = TRUE, reml=True), the default in both, because ML and REML give different variance components and so different standard errors.
Both: visit NUMERIC (a linear trend). As a factor it would estimate a separate difference at every visit.
Python: L-BFGS pgtol and factr tightened. At statsmodels' defaults the patient SD stopped 3.8e-5 short of the exact REML value; lme4 reached it to 1e-8.
_random_slopes: A random intercept alone assumes every patient changes at the same rate apart from treatment. When individual trajectories differ, add a random slope; otherwise the interaction's standard error is too small.
